title: Acts Interpretation Act 1954
version_kind: in force from 2024-02-01; the current in-force version on the retrieval date
converter: qld_convert.py (Legalese Commons conversion script, Python 3 html.parser; not kept in the repository)
conversion: HTML 'whole' view to UTF-8 plain text: Chapter/Part/Division/Schedule headings kept as tab-indented lines ('Part 1 — Name'); sections as '<number><TAB><heading>'; paragraph numbers kept; tables one row per line as '| a | b |'; amendment-history notes (class view-history-note), links, scripts and site chrome removed; attribution and unofficial-version notice prepended.
notes: The page text does not print an 'in force from' sentence.
The version date 2024-02-01 is read from the page's own 'View whole Act' link (/view/whole/html/inforce/2024-02-01/act-1954-003) and from PublicationDate=20240201000000 in its search links.
The landing page, fetched once on 2026-11-11 at 14:15:39 UTC, carries the same link and the same PublicationDate.
The site stamps its own pages with the Queensland local date (2026-11-12, data-server-time=20261112001130); this deposit uses the UTC date 2026-11-11 throughout.

The HTML embeds the request date in its links (143 occurrences of date=2026-11-12 in this download) and in data-server-time, so a download made on another day has a different sha256 although the Act text is the same.
The HTML view of this Act contains no tables, images, formulas or footnotes; nothing was left out for that reason.
Bold and italic marking in the HTML (for example of defined terms and of mentioned words) is not carried into the plain text.
The HTML has two unmatched end tags, in section 14CA(1) and (2), where the closing words are indented with non-breaking spaces; the words are kept and the indentation is not.
The Act has 144 section headings, numbered 1 to 58 with lettered insertions; 18 of them read '[Repealed]' and 2 read '[Expired]' (sections 15DB and 15DC), and none of these 20 carries any text.
Schedule 1 (the dictionary) lists 66 repealed definitions; the register shows each as the defined term followed by '...', and they are kept in that form.
Two amendment-history notes carry editorial wording rather than amendment references; they were removed with the other history notes.

The first, after the history of section 36, reads: 'Note—s 36 contained definitions for this Act. Definitions are now located in schedule 1 (Dictionary). Annotations for definitions contained in s 36 are located in annotations for sch 1.'
The second, at the end of schedule 1, reads: 'sch 1 Note—definitions for this Act were originally located in s 36.'

The same converter, run on a fresh download of the Civil Liability Act 2003 (act-2003-016), reproduced the text committed for that deposit byte for byte (sha256 2c8cbf78ced66ee1e759834912ef22a501cf77e7ccc5b0ffe94711551f766333).
